newsitem.title: USA: Taiwan news seen giving US hog prices $4-$5 boost.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan news seen giving US hog prices $4-$5 boost.

text.p: An increase of $4.00 to $5.00 per hundredweight in U.S. hog prices is likely for the rest of the year due to Taiwan's decision to ban pork exports, said Glenn Grimes, an agricultural economist at the University of Missouri.

Grimes based his forecast on the assumption that the U.S. would gain two-thirds of Taiwan's share of the Japanese pork export market, he said in a statement. In 1996 Taiwan exported 335,000 tonnes of pork to Japan, he said.
Taiwan banned pork exports earlier Thursday because of an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in the island's hog herd.
Grimes also noted marketing margins for pork were near record-high levels during February and the gap between retail pork and hog prices may narrow later in the year.
The combination of these two factors could cause live hog prices to rise as much as $13 to $14 per cwt, he said.
"At least 50 percent of this increase would be highly probable," Grimes said.
U.S. hogs in the Iowa-south Minnesota and Illinois interior markets traded at prices of up to $47.50 per cwt Thursday.
